documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are strong: published VIN that decodes cleanly, window sticker, clean CA title claim, Carfax, no-reserve terms. Some dated maintenance is said to be documented (tires with 2024 date codes, oil, pads, cam sensor), plus a cold-start video. Missing are the at-risk items: no brake fluid or coolant by date, no cooling-system or injector records, no DME/tune verification, pre-2025 history only via the Carfax. Capture was incomplete, so the gallery records were not examined here.

condition.rationale: Low mileage and documented recent tires and front pads support good condition. A bidder's PPI is reported 'very positive' but not shared. Disclosed flaws: chips on front surfaces, windshield chip, cracked and scratched rear bumper, interior wear and a misaligned vent louvre, and corrosion on underbody hardware. Water pump, thermostat and charge pipe are original at 13 years.

price_value.rationale: The current bid of $20,800 is below the $24,071 fair-value midpoint, but with 2 days left on a no-reserve rare-spec car it will likely close near or above fair value. Comps include a 60k-mile 135is at $23,750 and a 27k-mile 135i at $31,000. Cosmetic known work and the due cooling catch-up pull value slightly.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, fun, rain-proof coupe within the budget band, but it is not one of his candidate models. It is exactly the 'turbo BMW like the 335i' category he has deprioritized, sharing much of the N55 running-cost profile of the car he just sold.

logistics.rationale: Venice, CA is a moderate distance with a straightforward drive home. A PPI is demonstrably permitted, though the 2-day window is tight. CA title, so registration and smog should be feasible.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: rare 135is (586 built), 6-speed manual, Le Mans Blue, factory M Performance exhaust, low miles. Offsets are a black interior, an open differential, and non-original wheels and cosmetic mods (OEM Euro taillights are tasteful).

evidence.mission_note: A manual, weatherproof, genuinely fun coupe that fits the price band, but it is the deprioritized turbo-BMW type rather than an MX-5 RF, Z3 3.0/M or GTI. At best it is an off-list enthusiast option, not a target.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-consistent 2013 135is coupe with a 6-speed manual, about 30k miles, no reserve, and a clean CA title and clean Carfax claimed. Dated documentation reportedly covers 2024-coded tires, recent oil, front pads and an exhaust cam sensor. Observed issues are a cracked and scratched rear bumper of unexplained cause, windshield and front chips, interior wear, and corrosion on underbody hardware. The seller also confirms the original water pump and charge pipe at 13 years. A bidder's PPI was completed and is described as positive, but it is not shared. Brake fluid and coolant dates, the stock-software claim, pre-2025 owner history and airbag recall completion remain unverified. The current bid is below the fair-value midpoint, but a no-reserve rare manual 135is is likely to close considerably higher. Separately from the car's merits, it sits in the turbo-BMW category the buyer has deprioritized, and it is not one of his named target models.
